blurb: The Indo-Aryan sacrificial religion of rta and fire ritual (yajna), which over two millennia develops into Hinduism: Upanishadic philosophy, epic and Puranic devotion, temple worship, bhakti movements, and modern reform.

events.description: 1,028 hymns in Vedic Sanskrit composed by priestly families and preserved by exacting oral transmission. Centers on rta (cosmic order), sacrifice, and gods such as Indra and Agni.
events.title: Rig Veda

events.description: Dialogues shifting focus from sacrifice to knowledge of atman (the self) and brahman (ultimate reality), and to liberation from rebirth — the philosophical foundation of later Hindu thought.
events.title: Principal Upanishads composed

events.description: The two great Sanskrit epics are composed and expanded over centuries: vast story-cycles that carry dharma (duty, right order) into narrative form and reshape popular religion.
events.title: Mahabharata & Ramayana take shape

events.description: Krishna's dialogue with the warrior Arjuna, set within the Mahabharata: on duty, disciplined action, devotion, and liberation. It becomes Hinduism's most commented scripture.
events.title: Bhagavad Gita

events.description: The Puranas retell creation and the deeds of Vishnu, Shiva, and the Goddess, while temple worship, image veneration, and pilgrimage become central to Hindu practice.
events.title: Puranas & temple Hinduism

events.description: From the Tamil Alvars and Nayanmars onward, emotional devotion to a personal god — sung in local languages — spreads across India and reshapes Hindu practice around love of god.
events.title: Bhakti movements flourish

events.description: The philosopher Shankara systematizes Advaita (non-dualism): the self is not different from brahman. Traditionally dated 788–820 CE; many scholars place him a generation earlier.
events.title: Shankara & Advaita Vedanta

events.description: From the Brahmo Samaj (1828) and Vivekananda's address to the World's Parliament of Religions (1893) to the modern diaspora, Hindu movements reform, organize, and spread worldwide.
events.title: Reform movements & a global Hinduism

name: Vedic tradition & Hinduism
